content.goal: Set a timeout on every model call so nothing hangs forever.
content.why: A remote model call can hang; a timeout bounds it. This is basic resilient-service discipline. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 17, section 17.5.)
content.code:
# Give the client a request timeout:
client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"],
    base_url=os.environ["GROQ_BASE_URL"],
    timeout=30,   # seconds
)
content.verify: A call that would otherwise hang now fails after ~30s with a timeout error, which your retry logic can catch — rather than freezing the whole request.

content.goal: Retry only TRANSIENT failures with growing backoff.
content.why: Retry timeouts, 429 rate limits, and 5xx errors with a growing wait — but never retry a 401 or 400, which will never succeed. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 17, section 17.5, and Ch 3.)
content.verify: A simulated 429 triggers backoff-and-retry; a simulated 401 (bad key) fails immediately without wasting retries. Only transient errors are retried.

content.goal: Add a provider FALLBACK — if Groq fails, switch to NVIDIA NIM.
content.why: Because you coded against the common interface (Chapter 3), failing over from one provider to another is straightforward — the payoff of provider-agnosticism. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 17, section 17.5.)
content.verify: If the primary provider is unreachable or exhausted, ATLAS transparently switches to the backup and still answers. On a healthy primary, the backup is never touched.
content.troubleshoot: Fill in NIM credentials in .env for a real fallback. If you have only one provider, a smaller model, a cached answer, or a safe canned reply are valid fallbacks too.

content.goal: Cap steps and output length so one request cannot run away with your budget.
content.why: Caps protect cost and prevent runaway loops — a single request must not exhaust your quota. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 17, section 17.3.)
content.code:
# You already have max_steps in run_agent. Also cap output length per call:
#   robust_chat(messages, max_tokens=500, temperature=0)
# And keep the system prompt tight — it is re-sent every step, so every
# trimmed token is saved on every step (Chapters 2, 4).
content.verify: A task cannot exceed your step cap, and no single reply can balloon in length. Your trace's total-tokens count stays bounded per request.

content.goal: Make dangerous actions idempotent (safe to retry).
content.why: Since a request may be retried, a retried "delete" or "send payment" must not happen twice — use an idempotency key. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 17, section 17.5.)
content.verify: Calling a consequential action twice with the same key performs it only once — the second call reports "already done." Retries are now safe.

content.why: You have the resilient-service playbook applied to an LLM dependency.
content.verify: All true — every model call has a timeout; transient failures retry with backoff (but 401/400 do not); a provider fallback (Groq to NIM) keeps ATLAS answering; steps and output length are capped; consequential actions are idempotent.
